source.title: Understanding the Role of Optimization in Double Descent

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; some figure contents are flattened, and many plotted values are not numerically stated.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests model-wise double descent and refines its scope: it reports that the peak varies with conditioning and optimization, can be weak or absent, and can return with longer training.
record.gate_note: The paper reports plotted test-error-versus-size curves and explicit textual findings about when the peak appears, disappears, or returns. It also discusses epoch evolution, but does not report the test error of a fixed model as a fall-rise-fall curve over epochs. It does not sweep training-set size. Detailed numerical values for plotted curves are not stated.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps model size in random-feature models and two-layer networks on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10. It reports test-error curves where the peak appears, shrinks or disappears with conditioning and optimizer settings, then returns with 10x training. These are results on whether and when the model-wise curve holds, though without numeric tables.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors claim model-wise double descent occurs if and only if the optimizer finds a sufficiently low-loss minimum. They argue conditioning factors act through the condition number, and optimizer hyperparameters act directly on the minimum found. They note recovery needed 200–400x more training after zero training error. They conclude double descent is unlikely to be a problem in real-world setups, explaining weak peaks in practice.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses model-size sweeps and test error, with fixed hyperparameters in its default setup, but focuses on random-feature models and two-layer networks and systematically varies optimization, conditioning, and training duration. It does not reproduce the original study's broad deep-network scale settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported peak changes with normalization, feature scale, random-matrix initialization scale, learning rate and its decay frequency, batch size, optimizer, activation, and training duration.

fits_no_version.finding: The condition number peaks at P=N in every setting, but the test-error peak appears only when the optimizer reaches low training loss at P=N. Peak height tracks final training loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Double-descent peak height depends on whether the optimizer reaches a sufficiently low-loss minimum at the interpolation threshold.

record.peer_reviewed: OPT2023: 15th Annual Workshop on Optimization for Machine Learning; arXiv.org
record.problems: Many results are available only as plots without stated numerical values or uncertainty intervals. Experiments use random-feature models and two-layer networks; the authors do not test the sample-size claim or fixed-model epoch-wise curve. Some supplementary figure conditions are not numerically described in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Individual plotted values for every learning rate, decay interval, batch size, optimizer, and initialization/feature scale are not separately extracted; the text does not state those values numerically, and the curves are figure-only. Relevant sweeps are in Figures 1–3 and 6–11.

untested.parts: Deep networks beyond two layers; only RFMs and two-layer networks are tested.
Entirely untested: no fixed-model test error over epochs.
Entirely untested: no sweep of training-set size.
Non-neural model classes other than random-feature models (e.g., trees, kernels in general).
Varying label noise, variance as the driver, multiple or triple peaks, and optimally tuned regularization.

missing.what: Two-layer NN curves under normalization, feature scale, init scale, learning rate, decay and batch size, where the peak becomes less prominent
Sigmoid shows no double descent in two-layer NNs; mish and softsign show it only in RFMs, not two-layer NNs
Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 RFM curves for unnormalized, small-scale and small-init features
SGD and SAGA solvers show only a mild peak versus Cholesky's near-random peak

record.verdict_notes: All results are figure-only, with no numbers or error bars stated. It is a workshop paper. The paper's own unified criterion (a low-loss minimum) is an optimization account, not an effective-complexity measure in the V5 sense.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests model-wise curves in random-feature models and two-layer neural networks, not large modern deep networks generally.
No fixed-model test-error trajectory over training time is reported as a fall-rise-fall curve; the paper instead shows how the model-wise size curve changes across training epochs.
Training-set size is not swept to test whether adding samples near interpolation raises test error.
The study covers random-feature models and two-layer neural networks on image datasets, not model classes generally.
The paper relates peak height to optimization and training loss, but does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak location along size, epochs, and sample size.
The paper tests whether label noise is necessary by reporting double descent on clean datasets. It does not test multiple/triple peaks or optimally tuned regularization.
The paper does not re-count complexity using an effective number of parameters or test whether that turns the second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.
